$description: AudioSync's design tokens, shared by the macOS app, the Windows app and the website. Edit this file, then run python3 -I scripts/brand/tokens.py, which writes Sources/AudioSync/BrandTokens.swift, windows/ui/tokens.slint, windows/src/tokens.rs and the variable block in site/index.html.

color.$description: Each color has a light and a dark value (#RRGGBB). Where the two are the same, the color doesn't change with the appearance.

teal.description: Brand teal: the mark, the app accent, filled indicators. Only 3.27:1 on white, so never for small text.

mint.description: Brand mint: the mark and "sync" on dark backgrounds.

logo.description: The mark and "sync" in the wordmark: teal on light, mint on dark.

tealText.description: Teal for small text and text-sized glyphs (WCAG AA): 5.85:1 on white, 5.07:1 on #323232.

text.description: Body text: charcoal on light, off-white on dark (the wordmark's "audio").

muted.description: Secondary text on the website and the Windows app.

playingRow.description: A playing speaker's row: the brand teal at 8% on the surface, as on the Mac.

notice.description: Notice background: the Mac's orange notice tint (12%) on the surface.

separator.description: Card borders and dividers (decorative, no contrast requirement).

focus.description: Keyboard focus ring (3:1 against the surface and the background).

alpha.$description: Translucent colors: a base color at an opacity (0-1).

secondaryText.description: Secondary text on the Mac is the primary label color at this opacity: 5.59:1 on a light window, 6.64:1 on a dark one (Brand.swift).

disabled.description: Rows and controls that can't be used right now.

brand.description: The wordmark typeface (SIL OFL 1.1). Tracking is in em. User interface text uses the system font (SF Pro on macOS, Segoe UI Variable on Windows).

size.$description: Text sizes in logical pixels for the Windows app (the Windows type ramp). The Mac uses the system text styles; only its wordmark size (21 pt) comes from here.

spacing.$description: Distances in points (macOS) and logical pixels (Windows), as the Mac main window uses them.

radius.$description: Corner radii in points (macOS), logical pixels (Windows) and CSS pixels (website).

site.$description: The website's CSS variables, in order, and the token each one comes from. The site has one (light) appearance.

contrast.$description: Every text color on every background the Windows app draws it on. A unit test in windows/ fails when one is below 4.5:1, in either appearance. A foreground written as name@opacity is that color at that opacity.
